basics.name: Robert Schäfer
basics.label: Full Stack Developer
basics.summary: Freelance full stack developer working remotely across web applications, product engineering, and infrastructure, with additional investment in open source. Focus areas include maintainable software, strong test coverage, and modernizing fragile systems by simplifying delivery and operations while strengthening quality through reliable collaboration, code reviews, pair programming, and technical mentoring.

projects.name: Remote observatory
projects.description: With this platform for remotely controlling telescopes through the astrophotography software NINA, deep-sky imaging gets accessible without owning expensive hardware or the expertise to operate it. Users select an astronomical target and book observation time; the application sends imaging sequences to NINA via Tailscale, which executes them overnight and delivers the results. The core challenge is turning a Windows-only, inherently interactive application into a fully autonomous pipeline.

projects.name: AI interview platform
projects.description: This SvelteKit application for AI-assisted interviews and editorial publishing replaces brittle infrastructure spread across Airtable, Voiceflow, and additional custom services with a single serverless application. Using the built-in workflows of ElevenLabs AI Agents significantly reduces maintenance overhead and complexity while improving the phone agent's response time by several seconds, which is crucial for a good user experience.

projects.name: hledger-document-check
projects.description: A Plain Text Accounting command-line tool for checking documents with hledger. It reconciles transactions that require documentation with files on disk, detects missing or unbooked documents, checks amount plausibility, and generates an enriched journal for Fava's document view.

projects.name: hledger-elster
projects.description: A Plain Text Accounting command-line tool for hledger that automates German tax filing. It reads transactions from the journal and generates traceable exports for the corresponding forms on ELSTER.de. The exports are available in CSV and XLSX format and include derivations that tax authorities can audit.

projects.name: roschaefer.de
projects.description: Personal portfolio website and print-optimized resume built from a shared content source. The project combines a bilingual SvelteKit frontend, PDF generation with Typst, and standards-compliant `resume.json` into an accessible, privacy-conscious experience for web and print.

projects.name: FOSS social network
projects.description: Migrated assets from a Kubernetes volume to S3-compatible object storage to reduce deployment complexity and cost. Rebuilt the infrastructure with Terraform and sops, and moved from a managed Kubernetes cluster on Digital Ocean to a self-hosted Kubernetes cluster on Hetzner, cutting monthly costs by 80%.

projects.name: Founder network
projects.description: For this free and open-source social platform for entrepreneurs, the delivery and infrastructure architecture was fundamentally reworked after deployments had previously been performed manually via a remote desktop on the target server, regularly causing downtime. Moving the project to a self-managed Kubernetes setup on Hetzner with Terraform gave every developer production-like test environments for their own branches while keeping operating costs extremely low at under 20 euros per month.

projects.name: Booking website for a holiday apartment
projects.description: Built a booking website with calendar integration for a holiday apartment on Norderney. Day-by-day availability is maintained in Google Calendar and synchronized to the site via Google APIs.

projects.name: SvelteKit relaunch
projects.description: Rebuilt a retail client's website with SvelteKit and Hygraph and deployed it statically on Netlify. Server-side logic runs in serverless functions, and content is loaded from the headless CMS via GraphQL. The relaunch improved performance, SEO, and maintainability.

projects.name: Auto parts price comparison
projects.description: For this software for the automotive aftermarket that helps repair shops compare prices across wholesalers, an Electron desktop application was migrated to a cloud-based platform on Google Cloud, Auth0, and Hasura. This significantly improved software quality and increased the number of connected wholesalers from 3 to 240.

projects.name: Booking system for continuing education providers
projects.description: Built a custom booking system for a continuing education provider. The solution includes email confirmations, waiting lists, and an implementation based on SvelteKit with Hygraph as the headless CMS.

projects.name: Booking system for course providers
projects.description: Built a custom booking system for a course provider's sewing classes and integrated it into their website. Courses for adults, teens, and children can be managed online, including registration and waiting lists.

projects.name: Newsroom dialog
projects.description: For this platform for audience engagement and crowd-based reporting in journalism, the Ruby on Rails application integrates messengers such as WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Threema, and email, allowing editorial teams to reach people through channels they already use. Its core differentiator is a direct 1:1 conversation between journalists and their audience, turning a newsroom's own community into a valuable asset for reporting and research.

Bee sensor stories
projects.description: Building on an earlier journalistic sensor-data project, the platform was reused and extended for a new format. Reports were generated automatically from sensor data collected from three beehives. The project was nominated for the Grimme Online Award and won the German Reporter Award.

projects.name: Find open-source contributors in online learner communities
FOSS social network
projects.description: Technical Lead work on product architecture, GraphQL APIs, production use of Neo4J, and Kubernetes-based operations for a community-built open-source social network that offers communities a privacy-friendly alternative to large platforms. The project grew to around 80 code contributors on GitHub; newcomers were onboarded through GitHub, Discord, and online pair programming, mentored directly, and most contributions were reviewed. Neo4J ran in production as the primary database to model the network's social graph directly.
